clauses.reason: Operative on 2026-10-14. Section 1 designates the Department of State as the Central Authority of the United States for the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction and authorizes the Secretary of State to perform the acts necessary to execute those functions. The held text has no end date or condition, no held later instrument amends or revokes it, and the current U.S. Code still prints the order as a note to 22 U.S.C. 9006 with no amending or revoking instrument in the header line.

research_rationale:
EO 12648 (53 FR 30637, signed 1988-08-11, published 1988-08-15) is a one-section order. I read the held Federal Register text in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12648.txt, page 7 of the August 15, 1988 issue; its heading names Executive Order 12648 of August 11, 1988, 'Relating to the Implementation of the Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction'). The preamble recites that the Convention entered into force for the United States on July 1, 1988 and that the order is issued under section 7 of the International Child Abduction Remedies Act; section 1 designates the Department of State as the Central Authority of the United States and authorizes the Secretary of State to perform the acts needed to execute the Central Authority's functions. The held text has no sunset, condition, deadline or termination language. The current record is the U.S. Code editorial note printing the order under 22 U.S.C. 9006 note (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; laws enacted from 2026-10-10 through 2026-10-14 are not reflected in that edition); its header lists no amending or revoking instrument. The three bounded searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) found no later instrument that amends, revokes or supersedes the order, so no later event is attached. The held texts that cite the number are the order's own Federal Register text and the 1989 codification snapshot only. This is a claim on the held official Federal Register text; the 2026 predicate rests on the Code note and the bounded searches, not on a consolidated agency source.
